history.idea: Replace random order with a target-similarity filter plus dedup. Steps: (1) Fit a TfidfVectorizer on character n-grams (analyzer='char_wb', ngram_range=(1,3), sublinear_tf=True, max_features ~50k, on the first ~3000 chars of each doc) over target_sample (label 1) and a seeded random 3000-doc subsample of the pool (label 0); train LogisticRegression (C=1, max_iter=200) and score every pool doc with decision_function. (2) Add cheap WikiText-format features to rule out junk: hard-drop docs that do not start with '= ' (title line), docs shorter than 200 chars, and docs with a spam signature (contain 'discount code', 'coupon', 'free shipping', 'Click here to order'). (3) Detect word-shuffled docs (same Wikipedia vocabulary but scrambled order): build a set of word bigrams from target_sample, and for each pool doc compute the fraction of its first 400 word bigrams found in that set; also compute the fraction of ' , ' / ' . ' tokens that directly follow another punctuation token or start a line. Drop docs whose bigram-hit fraction falls below a threshold set at the 5th percentile of the same statistic measured leave-one-out on target_sample docs (each target doc scored against bigrams from the other 199). (4) Exact/near dedup: keep only the first doc per hash of the whitespace-normalised first 500 chars. (5) Rank survivors by classifier score, keep the top docs until their gpt2 token count (tiktoken encode_ordinary_batch, or estimated as len(chars)/4.3 if time is short) reaches about 1.0 T; if survivors total less than T, keep them all and let the trainer cycle. (6) Shuffle the kept indices with random.Random(int(os.environ.get('CURATE_SEED',0))) and return.
history.outcome: dev 1.8379 against 1.9630 for the best at the time, KEPT as the new best

history.idea: Replace the TfidfVectorizer character n-gram features with a Word2Vec-style approach or a higher-quality set of features, specifically by including document length and the presence of Wikipedia-style formatting (headers, lists, and specific punctuation patterns) as additional features for the LogisticRegression classifier.
history.outcome: dev 1.8403 against 1.8379 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: Replace the char_wb (1, 3) TfidfVectorizer with a combination of word-level n-grams (1, 2) and character-level n-grams (3, 5) while increasing the max_features to 75,000 and using a higher C value (C=10.0) for the LogisticRegression.
history.outcome: dev 1.8390 against 1.8379 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: Replace the LogisticRegression classifier with a simpler but more robust approach for this specific dataset: calculate the cosine similarity of the TF-IDF vectors of the pool documents against the centroid of the target_sample TF-IDF vectors.
history.outcome: dev 1.8384 against 1.8379 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: Replace the LogisticRegression classifier with a MaxEntropy (MultinomialNB) or a simplified SVM/LinearSVC approach, and increase the importance of the word-shuffle detection by making it a hard filter (dropping docs below the 10th percentile) rather than just a soft ranker, while also expanding the dedup window to the first 1000 characters.
history.outcome: dev 1.8250 against 1.8379 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: Instead of using the LogisticRegression decision_function as a pure ranker, implement a multi-stage filter: first, drop any document with a score below the 25th percentile of the pool; second, sort the remaining documents by score and select the top N such that their cumulative token count is ~1.05T; finally, apply a 'diversity' boost by ensuring that no more than 20% of the selected indices come from the top 10% of the ranked scores.
history.outcome: dev 1.8460 against 1.8379 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: Implement a 'density of high-quality markers' score: instead of just checking for the '= ' prefix, calculate a score based on the presence of Wikipedia-style structural elements (e.g., lines starting with '==', '===', or '---', and lines containing 'See also', 'References', or 'Categories') within the first 2000 characters, and use this as a secondary boosting feature in the LogisticRegression or as a hard threshold for documents that don't have a high classifier score.
history.outcome: dev 1.8373 against 1.8379 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: Refine the 'word-shuffle' detection and 'junk' filter by creating a 'quality score' for each document. This score will sum (1) the fraction of word bigrams matching the target sample's bigram set, (2) a penalty for common stop-word/punctuation 'bad' patterns, and (3) a bonus for the presence of specific Wikipedia-style structural markers (e.g., '==', '---', 'See also', 'References') in the first 2000 characters. Use this score as a weight for the LogisticRegression classifier or as a hard-filtering threshold at the 10th percentile.
history.outcome: dev 1.8250 against 1.8379 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: Replace the TfidfVectorizer character n-grams (1,3) with a more robust set of features: include character n-grams (2,4) and word n-grams (1,2), and add a binary feature for 'structural integrity' (presence of section headers like '==', '---', or '---' vs. junk artifacts like '@-@' or '!!!'). Use a LinearSVC instead of LogisticRegression to better handle the high-dimensional, sparse feature space and optimize for a harder margin.
history.outcome: dev 1.8317 against 1.8379 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: Replace the current TfidfVectorizer-based LogisticRegression with a two-stage ranking system: first, use a 'Quality Score' as a hard filter (top 50% of scores) where the score is a weighted sum of bigram hit rate, a penalty for 'bad' punctuation, and a bonus for Wikipedia-style structural markers (e.g., '==', '---', 'See also'); second, use the LogisticRegression decision_function to rank the remaining candidates, and select the top docs until reaching the token budget.
history.outcome: dev 1.8228 against 1.8379 for the best at the time, KEPT as the new best

history.idea: Replace the standard TfidfVectorizer (char_wb, 1, 3) with a more targeted approach: use the current TfidfVectorizer to select the top 10,000 'discriminative' terms (those with high variance in usage between target_sample and a random pool subsample) and then retrain the LogisticRegression using only these terms plus a high-weight binary feature for 'clean punctuation' (absence of '@-@', '!!!', or repeated punctuation like '...').
history.outcome: dev 1.8325 against 1.8228 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: Implement a 'Negative Sampling' improvement by constructing the negative set using a stratified approach: instead of a pure random sample, select 30% of the negatives from documents that pass the structural/spam filters but have low bigram overlap with the target sample, and 70% from completely random documents. Additionally, increase the LogisticRegression C parameter to 20.0 to encourage a harder margin on the high-quality subset.
history.outcome: dev 1.8314 against 1.8228 for the best at the time, rejected
